fatal_errors: The proposed HPHT treatment is unrelated to the target intervention of crystallographically oriented uniaxial tensile loading of single-crystal FCC FeNiCrMn.

The cited evidence concerns an Al0.7CoCrFeNi eutectic alloy containing both Al and Co, with a dual-phase FCC/B2 microstructure, so it does not support formation of the same microstructure in equiatomic Co-free FeNiCrMn.
The claimed validity over 77-1200 K and 10^8-10^10 s^-1 is unsupported by evidence obtained only from room-temperature tensile testing.
The hypothesis omits the target mechanisms of vacancy-associated dislocation nucleation, Shockley partial slip, and intrinsic/extrinsic stacking-fault formation.
It does not predict the target orientation anisotropy, temperature-induced yield softening, strain-rate-insensitive yield strength, or rate-dependent dislocation density and flow stress.
explanation: The response addresses the same nominal Co-free alloy and proposes a testable processing intervention, but it does not reconstruct the studied single-crystal dynamic-loading problem. Its mechanism and microstructure are transferred directly from a chemically and structurally different Al-Co-containing eutectic alloy. No evidence establishes that equiatomic FCC FeNiCrMn will develop coherent FCC/B2 interfaces under HPHT or that any resulting benefit persists at the stated temperatures and atomistic strain rates. The comparative falsification rule is directionally useful, but it is underspecified regarding crystallographic orientation, defect analysis, and discrimination among partial slip, stacking-fault formation, twinning, and phase transformation.
